_doc: Forced-skip anti-starvation fixture - FROZEN, READ-ONLY. Committed BEFORE the build run; hash-pinned by §10. Pins traffic scenarios the anti-starvation mechanism (MASTER-SPEC v7 §6.8, §11 step 5) is tested against. A build phase MUST NOT regenerate/edit it. Loader ignores keys beginning with '_'.
_scope: Declarative scenarios + pinned expected service schedules for a mechanism to be built in §11 step 5 and run against MaxPressureController (controllers.py). The ctor serves green[0]=phase0 at init (interval 0) BEFORE any decide(); therefore the STARVED phase is phase 1 (never served at init AND never wins _pressure argmax where LA>LB), so a no-override controller NEVER serves it -> assertion has teeth (fixes the ctor-init tautology).
_purpose: THREE discriminating checks so only a CORRECT per-phase-skip-counter mechanism passes: S1 constant single-starve (phase1 forced at the max_skip cadence); S2 alternating/reset-on-win (pressure flips so the starving phase changes AND a phase wins on pressure before max_skip, resetting its counter -> a hardcoded timer / global counter produces a DIFFERENT schedule); negative_control (running the mechanism with the override DISABLED on S1 MUST yield anti_starvation_violations>0 -> proves the counter is a live signal, not 0-for-free). Verified out-of-tree: correct mechanism reproduces the pinned schedules; no_override / modulo_timer / always_starved / over-eager(max_skip=2) each DIVERGE on >=1 scenario.
decision_interval: one decide() opportunity at a phase boundary; interval 0 = the ctor's initial green (phase0); intervals 1..N = successive decide() calls. Horizon = 10 intervals.

test_contract.counter_not_timer: the mechanism MUST derive force-service from a per-phase skip counter (incremented each interval a phase is eligible-but-unserved, RESET to 0 when the phase is served by EITHER argmax or override), NOT from a fixed interval timer. S2 distinguishes these.
test_contract.violations_read_not_set: the test READS controller.anti_starvation_violations; it MUST NOT assign it. The mechanism increments it when a phase's skip counter EXCEEDS max_skip (a starvation it failed to prevent).
test_contract.per_phase: skip counters are PER green phase (1:1 with approach here). A single global/modulo counter fails S2.
test_contract.safe_transition: force-service changes WHICH phase is served at a decision point; it MUST still honour min_green(10)+yellow(3) (S1/S2 invariants), never a mid-green interrupt.

scenarios._note: LA=9>LB=1 every interval -> phase0 wins argmax always; phase1 never wins and is not served at init -> starves; forced at the max_skip cadence.

LA=9/LB=1 for intervals 0-1 then FLIP to LA=1/LB=9: phase1 wins on PRESSURE at interval 2 (skip<max_skip, a reset-on-win, NOT an override), then phase0 starves and is FORCED later. A timer/global-counter yields a different schedule.
MUTATION test: run the mechanism with the anti-starvation override DISABLED on S1. This is NOT the correct mechanism; it proves the violations counter CAN be nonzero.

assertions: A. [S1] the anti-starvation controller serves phase1 (approach B) EXACTLY at [3, 7]; a no-override/timer-wrong controller diverges.
B. [S1] under plain MaxPressure.decide (no override) phase1 is NEVER served (pressure 1 vs 9) AND is not served at ctor-init (init serves phase0) -> establishes genuine starvation (has teeth).

C. [S2] the served schedule EXACTLY equals [0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0]: phase1 served on pressure at interval 2 (reset-on-win, not override) and phase0 FORCED later; a hardcoded timer or single global counter produces a different schedule.
D. [negative_control] with the override disabled on S1, anti_starvation_violations >= 1 and phase1 is never served -> the counter is a live signal, not 0-for-free.
E. [all] anti_starvation_violations == 0 EMERGES from the correct mechanism (never set by the test); each forced service respects min_green+yellow (S1/S2 invariants).
F. [contract] the test READS the counter; the mechanism derives service from the per-phase skip counter (reset on any service), NOT a timer -- S2 is the discriminator.
